method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reconstruction of both back-and-forth arguments and the quantifier-rank induction, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison after one documented source-correction projection. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Finite partial isomorphisms, the back-and-forth property, countable isomorphism, elementary equivalence in relational languages, quantifier rank, the finite-rank relations I_n and their equivalence with agreement on bounded-rank formulas.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A partial isomorphism is a finite partial injective map preserving every interpreted constant where defined, every predicate tuple and every function value on its domain. A nonempty family has the back-and-forth property when any source element can be added to a domain and any target element can be added to a range. For countable structures, alternating these extensions and taking their union yields an isomorphism.
samples.checks: Finiteness, all four preservation clauses, the empty-map observation, both extension directions, odd/even construction, increasing chain and union are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: In a purely relational language, partial isomorphism implies elementary equivalence by formula induction. With functions, one instead considers the induced isomorphism on generated substructures. Quantifier rank measures maximum nesting; n-equivalence means agreement on sentences of rank at most n, and a finite relational signature has only finitely many such sentences up to logical equivalence.
samples.checks: The relational-signature restriction, assignment pairing, n=0 sentence case, generated-substructure qualification, recursive rank definition, bounded-rank agreement and finite-signature proposition are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Finite domain sequences are extended by concatenation. I_0 records agreement on atomic formulas for corresponding tuple assignments; I_{n+1} requires every one-point extension on each side to have a matching extension on the other. M approximately_n N means I_n holds for their empty sequences, and I_n implies agreement on all formulas of rank at most n, with a converse for finite languages.
samples.checks: Sequence space, concatenation, equal-length condition, both I_n clauses, empty-sequence definition and theorem directionality are retained. OLFOL-027 separates tuple length k from recursion depth n.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The forward theorem direction is proved by formula induction. For the converse, rank zero reduces quantifier-free agreement to atomic agreement. At rank n+1, finite many inequivalent rank-n formulas allow their conjunction T_n^a to be existentially quantified, producing a matching element on the other side; symmetry supplies the reverse extension. Thus finite relational structures agree under I_n exactly when they are n-equivalent, and elementary equivalence is agreement at every finite rank.
samples.checks: Both inductions, finite-equivalence-class use, rank-zero base, existential witness step, symmetric back step and final biconditionals are retained.

source_observations: OLFOL-027 records a confirmed frozen-source collision between recursion depth n and sequence length: the I_0 atomic clause ended its variable list at x_n, which at n=0 excludes variables even for nonempty tuples. The target introduces common tuple length k and projects x_k back to x_n solely for source comparison.

The source uses two local conventions for purely relational language: the first theorem excludes functions and constants, while the later finite-signature proposition permits finitely many constants but no functions. The translation mirrors both parenthetical definitions rather than silently normalizing them.
MR-P124 directly attests प्रतांक for mathematical rank; partial-isomorphism and back-and-forth labels remain transparent source-defined compounds.
All other formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match the frozen source exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
